messages.content: What is the penalty for driving without a license under Section 181 of the Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act 2019?
Under Section 181, driving without a license now attracts a fine of 5000. Previously, the penalty was a fine of up to 500.
How has the penalty for over-speeding under Section 183(1) changed?

Previously, over-speeding carried a fine of up to 400. The new penalty is 1000 to 2000 for light motor vehicles (LMV) and 2000 to 4000 for medium passenger or goods vehicles. For a second or subsequent offence, the driving license can be impounded.
What are the new penalties for drunken driving under Section 185?

For a first offence, the fine is up to 10000 and/or imprisonment up to 6 months (previously a fine up to 2000 and/or imprisonment up to 6 months). For a second offence, the penalty is a fine of 3000 and/or imprisonment up to 2 years.
What is the penalty for not wearing a helmet under Section 194D?
Not wearing a helmet is a new provision under Section 194D. It carries a fine of 1000 and disqualification from holding a license for 3 months.
What does Section 194E say about emergency vehicles, and what is the penalty?
Section 194E, a new provision, penalises failure to allow free passage to emergency vehicles. The penalty is a fine of 10000 and/or imprisonment up to 6 months.
How is overloading of vehicles penalised under Section 194(1)?

The penalty is now a fine of minimum 20000 and 2000 per excess tonne, along with liability to pay for offloading. Previously it was a minimum of 2000 and 1000 per excess tonne, with liability to pay for offloading.
What are the penalties for dangerous driving under Section 184?

For a first offence, the penalty is now imprisonment of 6 months to 1 year and/or a fine of 1000 to 5000. For a subsequent offence within 3 years of the first, it is imprisonment up to 2 years and/or 10000. Earlier, a first offence meant imprisonment up to 6 months and a fine up to 1000.
What happens under Section 199A when a juvenile commits an offence?

Under this new provision, the guardian or owner is deemed guilty. The penalty is a fine of Rs. 25,000 and imprisonment up to 3 years, plus cancellation of the vehicle's registration for 12 months. The juvenile is also ineligible to obtain a learner's license until the age of 25 years.
What are the penalties for using a vehicle without a permit under Section 192A?

The new penalty for a first offence is imprisonment up to 6 months and a fine of 10,000. For a second offence, it is imprisonment between 6 months and 1 year and/or a fine of 10,000. The court has discretion to impose a lesser punishment.
What is the penalty for driving an uninsured vehicle under Section 196?

A first offence now carries a fine of 2000 and/or imprisonment up to 3 months. A second offence carries a fine of 4000 and/or imprisonment up to 3 months. Previously, the penalty was a fine of 1000 and/or punishment up to 3 months.
What does Section 194B say about safety belts and children?

Section 194B is a new provision. Failure to use safety belts and seating of children under 194B(1) carries a fine of 1000. Seating of children below 14 years under 194B(2) also carries a fine of 1000.
What is the penalty for using phones in silent zones under Section 194F?
Section 194F is a new provision. A first offence carries a fine of 1000, and a second offence carries a fine of 2000.
How can fines under the Act be revised over time?
Under Section 199B, fines can be increased annually by up to 10%. Additionally, under Section 210A, the State government can notify a multiplier between 1 to 10 for each fine.
What is the penalty for driving despite disqualification under Section 182(1)?
Driving despite disqualification now carries a fine of 10,000. Previously, the penalty was a fine up to 500.
What penalty applies to an enforcing authority that commits an offence under Section 210B?
Under Section 210B, a new provision, an offence committed by an enforcing authority is penalised at twice the penalty under the Act.
